lens: Documentation and onboarding cost. Inventory: CLAUDE.md (90 lines), README.md (307), knip.md (61, orphaned at root), docs/ top level 15 files (7,182 lines), docs/spec/ 18 files (3,509), docs/reference/ (00-decision-log.md 688 lines, studio-only-proposal.md 101, plus three binaries — reference-reel.mp4 5.3 MB, competitor-and-feature-plan-2026-09.docx 23 KB, original-business-case.pdf 11 KB — and 7 JPEG stills), docs/archive/ 6 files (851 lines), docs/wireframes/ 8 SVGs + index.html + make_wireframes.py (24 KB). Roughly 12,000 lines of prose, ~181k tokens if read whole. Measured read cost to ship one ticket safely, following the repo's own instruction (CLAUDE.md:15): CLAUDE.md + PROGRESS.md + NEXT.md = 2,741 lines, ~44,600 tokens — against the ~8k both CLAUDE.md:15 and NEXT.md:5 promise. Add README.md for commands and DEPLOYMENT.md or the item's spec doc and a realistic first ticket is ~3,900 lines / ~55k tokens before any code is opened. Of the pages a newcomer is pointed at first, I can demonstrate staleness in README.md (5 false claims), ARCHITECTURE.md (0/9 second-pass surfaces), USAGE-GUIDE.md (pre-second-pass, wrong domain), ROADMAP.md (4 of 7 'missing' items shipped), spec/README.md and spec/13-agent-runbook.md (old product name, pre-move paths, retired ticket IDs) — about 2,000 of the 7,182 top-level lines, and a higher share of the specific pages the entry instructions name. This is not a documentation-poverty problem; it is a documentation-surplus problem with no retirement discipline. Five claims checked against code, all five false: 'pnpm test | 168 unit and component tests' (README.md:80 — 659, per NEXT.md:27); 'The Supabase driver has never run' (README.md:295 — production runs DATA_DRIVER=supabase, CLAUDE.md:63); 'Phase 1 modules are not built' (README.md:303 — modules/registry.ts:29-32 registers all four); 'It applies both migrations' (README.md:201 — supabase/migrations holds 24, and scripts/bootstrap-supabase.ts:21 readdirSyncs them all); 'process.env only in lib/env.ts | eslint no-restricted-properties' (CLAUDE.md:30 — middleware.ts:23,34,74 violates it four times and pnpm lint reports clean). CONSOLIDATION PROPOSAL — one entry point, ten files instead of thirty-nine. (1) ONE ENTRY POINT: CLAUDE.md, ~120 lines, carrying the reading order for humans and agents alike; delete the competing 'start here' lines at README.md:20, docs/README.md:10, docs/README.md:17, CLAUDE.md:3-4 and spec/README.md:27. Fix PROGRESS.md:8 to match CLAUDE.md:15 (they disagree on the order of the same two files). (2) MERGE: fold docs/USAGE-GUIDE.md (521 lines, stale) into docs/MANUAL-TEST.md (423, current) as a 'what each feature is' preamble, keeping one operator-facing document; fold docs/REQUIREMENTS.md and docs/ROADMAP.md into docs/PRODUCT.md as a 'Target' column beside the existing Built/Partial/Missing, removing two of the four competing status paragraphs; fold docs/PRICING-MODEL.md into an appendix of docs/PRICING.md and delete the price tables from ROADMAP.md and REQUIREMENTS.md so one file owns the ladder. (3) ARCHIVE: move docs/GO-LIVE.md to docs/archive/go-live-aug-sept-2026.md (three completed runbooks in one file, three H1s, titled for a retired domain), move the pre-second-pass docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to docs/archive/ and rewrite it from spec/16-platform-v2.md plus the code, move docs/COMPETITORS.md and docs/SCALE-PLAN.md into docs/reference/ (read once when planning, not on the way in). (4) DELETE: docs/spec/README.md and docs/spec/13-agent-runbook.md (both describe a ticket scheme, a file layout and a product name that no longer exist; doc 13's value — the per-ticket reading budget — survives as three lines in CLAUDE.md); knip.md moves next to knip.json or into docs/reference/. (5) REGENERATE, DO NOT MAINTAIN: docs/spec/07-api-contracts.md covers 13 of 60 routes; replace it with a generated route index from the app/api tree. (6) GIT-LFS or drop docs/reference/reference-reel.mp4 (5.3 MB binary in every clone). Result: CLAUDE.md -> PRODUCT.md -> NEXT.md as the living path (~1,000 lines), PROGRESS.md as an append-only log nobody reads on the way in, spec/ frozen as history with its existing superseded banners, everything else in reference/ or archive/. Target cold start: under 10k tokens, and true this time.
strengths: The in-code documentation is the best documentation in this repository, and it is not close. lib/catalogue-access.ts:8-14 states the invariant ('the one place a guest request is authorised') and names the three rules that cannot be re-implemented three ways; modules/registry.ts:14-19 states its own contract; app/api/admin/credits/route.ts:8 cites the decision (D-38) that produced the endpoint. At 15% comment density and consistently 'why' rather than 'what', an engineer who read only the code would be better informed than one who read only docs/.

docs/spec/16-platform-v2.md:9-14 is a model status banner and should be the template for every document in the tree: each section mapped to the ticket that built it, the migration range named (0016-0025), and — the part almost nobody writes — the three specific places the shipped thing differs from the spec.

The superseded-banner convention (docs/spec/01-product-spec.md:222, docs/spec/02-information-architecture.md:8, docs/spec/11-whitelabel-and-b2b.md:42, docs/spec/15-partners-and-scale.md:101) annotates rather than rewrites, so the reasoning survives even where the numbers do not. docs/README.md:35-40 argues for this explicitly. It is a rare and correct instinct.

docs/PROGRESS.md:18-41, 'Lessons that still bind', is the single highest-value page in the repository and it is 24 lines: eight non-obvious rules, each traceable to a specific real failure (playback tokens sign the directory not the manifest; tus gives up on a bare network error without onShouldRetry; never delete and recreate a Supabase auth user to change a password). Distilling the Phase 0 log down to this instead of leaving 491 lines in the read path was the right call.

The documentation tells you how things break, not only how they work — README.md:209-212 warns that Bunny's user.insufficient_balance reads like a permissions error and is not one; docs/MANUAL-TEST.md:41-62 explains that a platform admin needs both the auth account and the platform_admins row and that having one looks exactly like the console being broken. That class of writing saves hours and is rarer than it should be.

The four .claude/skills encode workflow as executable procedure rather than prose, and .claude/skills/next-item/SKILL.md:40-44 writes down a standard most teams never articulate: prove a check by breaking the thing it guards; cover the code, not the markup; never report completion on a partial run.

The context-discipline instinct in CLAUDE.md is right even where its arithmetic is wrong. A 90-line root instruction file that says what to read, in what order, and what never to read (CLAUDE.md:20-21) is better than what most repositories this size have.

findings.title: The ship skill's 'confirm it is actually live' step checks a host the backlog itself calls luck
findings.evidence: .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md:46 is `curl -s https://marquee-film-pub.vercel.app/api/health`, and lines 49-51 say to treat a matching `version` as proof the deploy landed. Production is elsewhere: scripts/deploy-vercel.sh:26 reads `PROJECT="${VERCEL_PROJECT:-mehfilbox}"` and docs/MANUAL-TEST.md:413 curls `https://mehfilbox.com/api/health`. The repository already knows this host is unsafe — docs/PROGRESS.md:422-425 records that renaming the Vercel project orphaned the alias and `marquee-film-pub.vercel.app` 'kept serving the previous commit, silently', and docs/NEXT.md:476-478 says it is 'still attached and still serving the current build — luck rather than design. The alias list already holds several `marquee-film-*` names pinned to deployments days old.'
findings.why_it_matters: The ship skill exists to close exactly one gap, stated in its own first line: 'Committed is not deployed.' Its final gate points at a legacy alias that has already served a stale commit once and is pinned by luck. A hotfix on a wedding day can be reported live, with a version hash and a green driver line, while mehfilbox.com serves the old build. That is a customer-visible failure disguised as a successful verification.
findings.fix: In .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md:46 replace the URL with `curl -s https://mehfilbox.com/api/health`, and add a second line checking the deployment URL that scripts/deploy-vercel.sh prints, so both the canonical domain and the fresh deployment are compared to HEAD. While there, grep the tree for `marquee-film-pub` and fix or delete the other live references (docs/GO-LIVE.md:236, docs/NEXT.md:476); the ones in docs/PROGRESS.md and docs/archive/ are history and should stay.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's 'enforced rather than remembered' table is false for middleware.ts, modules/ and themes/ — pnpm lint never visits them
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:25-26 promises 'These are lint rules, tests or types, not conventions... the check will tell you before review does', then CLAUDE.md:30 claims `process.env` only in lib/env.ts is enforced by eslint `no-restricted-properties`. package.json:14 defines `lint` as bare `next lint`, and node_modules/next/dist/lib/constants.js:291 sets ESLINT_DEFAULT_DIRS to ['app','pages','components','lib','src'] only. I ran both: `pnpm lint` prints 'No ESLint warnings or errors', while `pnpm exec next lint --file middleware.ts` reports four `no-restricted-properties` errors at middleware.ts:23, 34, 74 and 74. The same blind spot covers modules/ (2,213 lines, 40 files — the product's stated moat), themes/ (382 lines) and every root config file, so CLAUDE.md:31 (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML) and the eslint half of CLAUDE.md:32 (no `any`) are unchecked there too; tsconfig.json:7 gives `strict` but strict TypeScript permits an explicit `any`.
findings.why_it_matters: middleware.ts is the file that decides which tenant a request resolves to, and it is the one file in the product with no lint coverage at all. Worse than the gap is the documentation: an engineer who reads CLAUDE.md believes the guard exists and stops checking by hand. A configuration read that bypasses lib/env.ts validation in the tenancy router is precisely the class of bug docs/PROGRESS.md:24-26 says has already cost this project three fatal production faults, all of them configuration and all of them past a green suite.
findings.fix: Change package.json:14 to `next lint --dir app --dir components --dir lib --dir modules --dir themes --file middleware.ts` (or migrate to the ESLint CLI, which next lint:1 already warns is required for Next 16), then fix the four middleware.ts violations or add them to the .eslintrc.json:27 override list deliberately. Then correct the CLAUDE.md:28-37 table so each row says what is actually covered — a rule that is true in four directories and silent in three is worse documentation than no rule.

findings.title: README.md's 'Known gaps' section describes a prototype; the shipped product is a phase ahead of it
findings.evidence: README.md:295-297 states 'The Supabase driver has never run. SupabaseRepository and both migrations still have no execution behind them' — CLAUDE.md:63 says 'production runs on it', docs/NEXT.md:30 confirms `DATA_DRIVER=supabase`, and supabase/migrations holds 24 files (0001 through 0025), not two. README.md:303-304 states 'Phase 1 modules are not built. continue_watching, timeline, checklist, randomiser are Phase 1 by plan' — modules/registry.ts:29-32 registers all four, each has its own folder, and docs/PROGRESS.md:354 is the entry that built them. README.md:201 says the bootstrap script 'applies both migrations'; scripts/bootstrap-supabase.ts:21 readdirSyncs the whole directory. README.md:80 advertises '168 unit and component tests'; docs/NEXT.md:27 and docs/PROGRESS.md:2050 both say 659. README.md:166 says `mehfilbox.in` redirects while docs/NEXT.md:30 says `heirloomfilms.in` does.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the file a contractor, an acquirer, a co-founder or a future you opens first, and it is the file that would most shape a rewrite decision. It understates the test suite by a factor of four, declares the database integration unproven when production has run on it since 12 September, and says four shipped modules do not exist. A new engineer reading it would rebuild work that already exists; anyone assessing the codebase would conclude it is less finished than it is.
findings.fix: Rewrite README.md:275-307 from docs/PRODUCT.md §8 and docs/NEXT.md's Tier 1c, deleting the four gaps that closed and keeping the three that are still real (dynamic browse route, cookie-based operator auth, no Lighthouse/QoE gate in CI). Replace the hardcoded '168' at README.md:80 with 'the unit and component suite' so no number needs maintaining, and fix README.md:201 to 'applies every migration in supabase/migrations, in order'. Then add one line at the top of the Known gaps section giving the date it was last checked, so the next reader knows what they are trusting.

findings.title: The two files CLAUDE.md tells you to read first are the most stale documents in the tree
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:3-4: 'Read docs/spec/README.md first, then docs/spec/13-agent-runbook.md §2 for the per-ticket reading map.' docs/spec/README.md:1 is titled 'Heirloom Films — build documentation' (renamed to Mehfilbox on 7 September, D-23). Its file map at lines 45-69 uses pre-move paths throughout (`docs/00-INDEX.md`, `docs/09-implementation-plan.md`, `scripts/make_wireframes.py`) — everything moved under docs/spec/ and the script lives at docs/wireframes/make_wireframes.py, so the command at line 105 fails. Line 63 describes the decision log as 'D-1 … D-9'; it runs to D-44. docs/spec/13-agent-runbook.md §2 (lines 19-45) maps only tickets P0-01 through P0-30, all retired — the live backlog is N-nn in docs/NEXT.md — with the same wrong paths, and its ready-to-paste prompt at line 65 runs `pnpm lint && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test`, which skips check:dead and check:contrast that package.json:24 makes part of `pnpm verify`.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the literal first instruction in the repository's own instruction file, and following it costs a new engineer or agent their first hour on a map of a codebase that no longer exists, under a product name that was retired, with a verification command weaker than the one the project actually requires. Worse, CLAUDE.md:15 gives a different reading order eleven lines later, so the file contradicts itself before the reader reaches the rules.
findings.fix: Delete CLAUDE.md:3-5 and make CLAUDE.md:14-15 the only reading order. Move docs/spec/README.md and docs/spec/13-agent-runbook.md to docs/archive/, keeping doc 13's one surviving idea — never load the whole doc set; load what the item names — as two lines under CLAUDE.md's Context discipline heading. docs/spec/00-INDEX.md:29 already carries that warning and can stay as the spec tree's own front page.

findings.title: The advertised cold start is wrong by 5.6x, and it is the number the whole context-discipline argument rests on
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:14-15: 'Read CLAUDE.md → PROGRESS → NEXT; a cold start is then ~8k tokens regardless of repo size.' docs/NEXT.md:5 repeats it verbatim. Measured: CLAUDE.md is 4,692 bytes (~1,200 tokens), docs/PROGRESS.md 136,276 bytes / 2,050 lines (~34,000 tokens), docs/NEXT.md 37,452 bytes / 601 lines (~9,400 tokens) — ~44,600 tokens for the mandated path. docs/spec/README.md:39 makes the stronger claim that PROGRESS.md alone 'lets a fresh session cold-start in ~4k tokens no matter how big the codebase gets'; it is 34k. .claude/skills/next-item/SKILL.md:13 prescribes the same three files.
findings.why_it_matters: The claim is the justification for the whole documentation structure, so being wrong about it is self-undermining: an agent or engineer budgets 8k, spends 45k, and arrives at the actual ticket with two-thirds of the window gone — which is the exact failure docs/spec/13-agent-runbook.md:9-11 was written to prevent. PROGRESS.md has grown to 62 entries and will keep growing; every new ticket makes the number more wrong while the document still claims it is constant.
findings.fix: Split docs/PROGRESS.md at line 1620 (the N-60 boundary): everything before it becomes docs/archive/progress-aug-sept-2026.md, and PROGRESS.md keeps the 'Lessons that still bind' block (lines 18-41) plus the most recent phase. Then change the reading order in CLAUDE.md:14-15, docs/NEXT.md:5 and .claude/skills/next-item/SKILL.md:13 to CLAUDE.md → PRODUCT.md → NEXT.md, and state the real measured number. Add a `pnpm docs:budget` script that wc -c's the three files and fails over a threshold, so the number cannot rot again.
findings.effort: 3-4 hours including the split and the script

findings.title: Five competing entry points, two of which contradict each other on the order of the same two files
findings.evidence: README.md:20 calls docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 'How it fits together, with diagrams — **start here**'. docs/README.md:9-10 puts PRODUCT.md first and calls ARCHITECTURE.md 'The best single entry point'; docs/README.md:17 adds 'Start here for anything commercial' for PRICING.md. CLAUDE.md:3-4 says read docs/spec/README.md first. CLAUDE.md:14-15 says 'Read CLAUDE.md → PROGRESS → NEXT'. docs/PROGRESS.md:8 says 'A fresh agent session reads CLAUDE.md → NEXT.md → this file' — the reverse of CLAUDE.md:15 for the same two files. .claude/skills/next-item/SKILL.md:13 gives a sixth. docs/spec/README.md:27 gives a seventh.
findings.why_it_matters: Every reader picks a different door, and two of the doors disagree about which of PROGRESS and NEXT comes first — which matters, because NEXT.md:5's status paragraph is the thing that tells you whether PROGRESS is still true. The cost is not confusion so much as inconsistency between sessions: two engineers, or two agent runs, arrive with materially different pictures of the same repository and neither knows it.
findings.fix: Pick one: CLAUDE.md → docs/PRODUCT.md → docs/NEXT.md. Delete the 'start here' phrasing from README.md:20 and docs/README.md:10 and:17, delete CLAUDE.md:3-5, correct docs/PROGRESS.md:8 to match, and reduce docs/README.md to a one-screen index that says which file owns which question and points at CLAUDE.md for the order. Every other document's opening paragraph should link to the entry point rather than assert its own.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md, named the 'best single entry point' in two places, predates a third of the shipped surface
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md was last modified 12 August 2026 and its nine sections (lines 1, 10, 55, 94, 129, 158, 179, 204, 234, 244) contain zero occurrences of credits, themes, house styles, platform console, custom domains, couple accounts, premiere, wizard or occasions — the entire second pass of 12 September, which docs/spec/16-platform-v2.md:9-14 records as N-60 through N-75 and migrations 0016-0025. Those surfaces are not small: credits touch 20 app files, 11 lib files and 11 components; 'platform' touches 30, 18 and 17; domains 17, 16 and 10. Its diagram at lines 17-22 shows three Vercel boxes and two crons for a product that now has 40 pages, 60 API routes and a platform console. Yet README.md:20 and docs/README.md:10 both send newcomers there first.
findings.why_it_matters: It is the only document that draws the system rather than listing it, so it is the one a new engineer will trust most and the one they will carry as their mental model. A model missing the platform console, the org credit ledger and the custom-domain path will produce design decisions that fight the code — most dangerously around org scoping, since platform admins sit outside the org model that ARCHITECTURE.md:83-88 explains so well.
findings.fix: Add three sections to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, sourced from docs/spec/16-platform-v2.md and the code: the platform console and where it sits relative to the org boundary (lib/admin/session.ts), the credit ledger and its writes, and the custom-domain resolution path alongside the existing tenant path. Until that is done, change README.md:20 and docs/README.md:10 to say the document covers the first pass only and name its date — a dated document is usable, an undated stale one is not.

findings.title: USAGE-GUIDE.md is a 521-line duplicate of MANUAL-TEST.md, three weeks older and describing a console since rebuilt
findings.evidence: docs/USAGE-GUIDE.md (521 lines, last modified 16 August) and docs/MANUAL-TEST.md (423 lines, 12 September) walk the same sixteen workflows in the same order — registration, create, films, photographs, customizer, publish, handover, platform admin. USAGE-GUIDE.md:6 asserts it 'describes what the software does today'; it contains zero mentions of themes, house styles or the premiere, one of 'wizard', and USAGE-GUIDE.md:10 still states 'The product lives at heirloomfilms.in'. The console it describes was rebuilt twice since — docs/PROGRESS.md:77 ('The console, rebuilt around what an operator is deciding') and docs/PROGRESS.md:1951 ('N-69 · Wizard v2'). docs/README.md:16 lists it as a live document, and docs/MANUAL-TEST.md:7 defers to it for 'what each feature is'.
findings.why_it_matters: Two documents claiming to describe today's product, one of them a month out of date and cross-referenced by the current one, means an operator or a new engineer following the older path hits screens that no longer exist and concludes the software is broken. It is also the document most likely to be sent to a first studio customer.
findings.fix: Merge the still-true conceptual sections of docs/USAGE-GUIDE.md (§1 Roles, §15 Limits and entitlements) into docs/MANUAL-TEST.md as a short preamble, delete the rest, remove the row at docs/README.md:16, and fix the dangling reference at docs/MANUAL-TEST.md:7. One operator-facing document, dated at the top, is worth more than two.

findings.title: Three product-shape documents each declare they deliberately disagree, and each is separately wrong about the current state
findings.evidence: docs/PRODUCT.md:3-8 ('the canonical list of what this product is'), docs/ROADMAP.md:8-12 ('the destination'), docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:3-5 ('the target, not the built product... disagrees with PRODUCT.md deliberately'), plus the status paragraphs at docs/NEXT.md:20-44 and docs/GO-LIVE.md:14 — five places a reader can learn 'where things stand'. Each is separately stale: docs/PRODUCT.md:16 says 'Last reviewed: 14 August 2026' and docs/PRODUCT.md:30 asserts 'The domain is still heirloomfilms.in', contradicting docs/NEXT.md:30 ('Live on https://mehfilbox.com'); docs/ROADMAP.md:18 says the product is 'deployed on heirloomfilms.in' and lines 22-24 list 'application email, payment, renewal, lapse, archive, metering, plan assignment' as not existing, though docs/PROGRESS.md:699 (email), :1327 (lapse notices), :1398 (plans) and the 12 September credits work shipped at least four of the seven; docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:3 anchors to 'D-11 to D-22' when docs/reference/00-decision-log.md runs to D-44.
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md:11-12 makes docs/PRODUCT.md the file to update before NEXT.md and before code, so its accuracy is load-bearing for the whole process — and it is wrong about the production domain, the single most checkable fact in the product. With five status paragraphs and no ownership rule, every reader gets a different answer and nobody is responsible for reconciling them.
findings.fix: Make docs/PRODUCT.md the only status document: add a 'Target' column beside Built/Partial/Missing so ROADMAP's destination and REQUIREMENTS' target live in the same table as reality, then move docs/ROADMAP.md and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md to docs/archive/. Fix docs/PRODUCT.md:30 and update the 'Last reviewed' line. Reduce docs/NEXT.md:20-44 to two sentences that link to PRODUCT.md rather than restating it.

findings.title: The API contract document covers 13 of 60 routes and none of the platform surface, but the index still sends form work there
findings.evidence: docs/spec/07-api-contracts.md (179 lines, last modified 8 August) mentions 13 distinct /api paths: admin/catalogues, admin/titles, admin/titles/reorder, admin/uploads, module-state, og, passcode, playback/token, profiles, progress, webhooks/bunny, webhooks/razorpay. The tree holds 60 route.ts files, including the whole platform console (/api/admin/platform/orgs/[id]/credits, .../quota, .../status, .../themes, .../operators/[id]/password-link), credits, domains and their checks, deliver, transfer, couple and photos. docs/spec/00-INDEX.md:13 lists doc 07 as answering 'Endpoints, request/response, validation, errors — Read before Form work'. No other document carries a route list: grep for 'api/admin/catalogues' across docs/*.md and docs/spec/*.md matches only doc 07.
findings.why_it_matters: Forty-seven routes have no written contract anywhere, and the index promises one. An engineer wiring a form against the credits or domains API follows the pointer, finds nothing, and either reads 60 files or guesses. The gap is survivable today only because the route files are unusually well commented (app/api/admin/credits/route.ts:8 names the decision behind the endpoint) — which is an argument for generating the index from them, not for keeping a hand-written one that covers a fifth of the surface.
findings.fix: Replace docs/spec/07-api-contracts.md with a generated docs/API.md: a script that walks app/api/**/route.ts, extracts the exported method names and the leading JSDoc line each already carries, and emits a table of path, methods and one-line purpose. Wire it into `pnpm verify` so it regenerates and fails on drift. Keep doc 07 in spec/ as history with a superseded banner, the way docs/spec/02-information-architecture.md:8 already does for addressing.
findings.effort: 4-6 hours for the generator, then it maintains itself

findings.title: Four unsynchronised documents carry live-looking prices and no price exists in code, so nothing can test the ladder
findings.evidence: docs/PRICING.md (378 lines, 58 distinct rupee figures), docs/PRICING-MODEL.md (587 lines, over 100 figures), docs/ROADMAP.md (19 figures) and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md (20 figures) all carry prices; docs/spec/11-whitelabel-and-b2b.md carries the retired ₹4,000/₹7,000/₹14,000/₹249 model but is correctly banner-marked at line 42. The ladder decided in docs/reference/00-decision-log.md:295 (D-17: Deliver ₹1,999, Keep ₹6,000, Cinema ₹12,000) appears in four files that must be edited together by hand. Grepping lib/ for price or amount constants returns nothing but a comment at lib/env.ts:89 — no tier price is a value in code, so no test can assert any of them.
findings.why_it_matters: Pre-revenue this is free; the first time a price changes it is four hand edits with no check, and the first time a customer is quoted from a stale table it costs the difference. docs/README.md:35-38 already identifies pricing as 'the largest divergence' between the trees — and then leaves four live copies rather than one.
findings.fix: Make docs/PRICING.md the only document with prices; strip the tables from docs/ROADMAP.md and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md down to links, and fold docs/PRICING-MODEL.md in as an appendix so the working-out sits under the answer. When billing lands (N-20, Razorpay), put the three tier amounts in lib/plans.ts and have a unit test assert the document matches — the same pattern tests/unit/contrast.test.ts already uses for palette values.
findings.effort: 3 hours now, plus 1 hour when billing lands

findings.title: GO-LIVE.md is three completed runbooks stacked in one file, titled for a retired domain, and the backlog still routes an open item to it
findings.evidence: docs/GO-LIVE.md has three top-level H1s — line 1 'Go live on heirloomfilms.in', line 317 'The Mehfilbox switch (N-52)', line 392 'The second pass, deployed — 12 September 2026' — appended rather than merged. Its section headings carry completion markers (line 49 '## 2. Point the domain at Vercel — ✅ done', line 213 '## 4. The switchover — ✅ done, except the webhook', line 359 '## 3. The switch — ✅ complete, 7 September'), and it holds 32 references to the retired name. docs/NEXT.md:464 still points a live backlog item at it: 'N-11 · Domain · **live** — one item left, see GO-LIVE.md §4' — ambiguous, since there are three §4s. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:287-289 has the same problem in miniature, verifying against admin.raammcorp.in and marquee.raammcorp.in, a domain from two renames ago.
findings.why_it_matters: 455 lines of completed history are indexed at docs/README.md:15-level prominence and cross-referenced from the live backlog, so a reader chasing the one remaining webhook item reads three migrations to find it. It also makes the deployment story look unfinished to anyone evaluating the repo, when in fact the deployment is done.
findings.fix: Move the finished halves to docs/archive/go-live-aug-sept-2026.md, lift the single open webhook item (docs/GO-LIVE.md:225-246) into docs/NEXT.md as its own N-item with the steps inline, and delete the cross-reference at docs/NEXT.md:464. Fix the stale hosts at docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:287-289 to mehfilbox.com in the same pass.

findings.title: Counting and numbering errors throughout make the documentation untrustworthy in the small
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:43 says 'Three workflows are encoded in .claude/skills/' above a four-row table (lines 47-50) and four SKILL.md files. The spec document count is given three ways: README.md:23 'docs 01–16', docs/README.md:26 'docs 01–15', .claude/skills/next-item/SKILL.md:16 'The spec is 17 documents'; there are 18 files. The decision log is described as 'D-1 … D-9' at docs/spec/README.md:63 and 'D-11 to D-22' at docs/README.md:27 and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:3; it runs to D-44, and contains two different decisions both numbered `## D-32` (docs/reference/00-decision-log.md:539 and :562), after which docs/NEXT.md:54 cites a range 'D-32 to D-41' that does not line up. docs/spec/00-INDEX.md:45-49 still instructs a trademark search on 'Heirloom Films' before public launch — a name retired 7 September and a site already live — and its glossary at line 37 addresses a catalogue as aanya-vikram.heirloomfilms.app, though docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:193 records subdomain mode as 'retired, kept for the harness'.
findings.why_it_matters: Individually trivial; collectively they teach the reader that no number in this documentation can be trusted without checking, which is exactly the habit that makes the accurate parts worthless too. The duplicate D-32 is the one with real cost: two decisions share an identifier that four other documents cite by number.
findings.fix: Renumber the second D-32 at docs/reference/00-decision-log.md:562 to the next free number, fix the citing ranges in docs/NEXT.md:54, docs/README.md:27 and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:3, correct CLAUDE.md:43 to 'Four workflows', and settle the spec count in one place. Add a line to the decision log's header stating that entries are append-only and numbers are never reused. Delete docs/spec/00-INDEX.md:45-49 and fix the glossary address at line 37.

findings.title: Orphaned and unindexed files: a root-level doc nothing links to, a 5.3 MB binary in every clone, and a generator with the wrong path
findings.evidence: knip.md (61 lines) sits at the repository root, referenced by neither README.md nor docs/README.md, and knip.md:11 records framer-motion as removed for having 'zero imports anywhere in the codebase' — while next.config.ts:26 still lists it in optimizePackageImports and package.json no longer holds it. docs/reference/reference-reel.mp4 is 5,332,102 bytes of video in git, which every clone and every CI checkout pays for, alongside a .docx and a .pdf that no text search can reach. docs/wireframes/make_wireframes.py (24,775 bytes) regenerates eight SVGs that CLAUDE.md:20 and docs/spec/13-agent-runbook.md:51 both tell you never to read, and the command to run it at docs/spec/README.md:105 gives the wrong path (`scripts/make_wireframes.py`).
findings.why_it_matters: None of these will break anything, but each is a small tax: the knip.md/next.config.ts mismatch means the document explaining the dead-code gate is itself carrying a dead reference, and a 5.3 MB binary in a repository whose documented virtue is a two-second test suite is an odd thing to make every clone carry.
findings.fix: Remove 'framer-motion' from next.config.ts:26 and move knip.md next to knip.json or into docs/reference/, linking it from docs/README.md. Move docs/reference/reference-reel.mp4 to git-lfs or to shared storage with a link, keeping the seven extracted JPEG stills in the repo since doc 14 §1 describes them. Fix the path at docs/spec/README.md:105, or delete the wireframe generator along with the SVGs nobody is permitted to read.
